chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from one of his companions from Aban from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who divorced his wife once, then took her back before her waiting period expired, and did not bear witness to his taking her back. He (peace be upon him) said: 'She is his wife as long as her waiting period has not expired, and it was befitting for him to bear witness to his taking her back. So if he was ignorant of that, let him bear witness when he knows, and I do not see any harm in what he has done. And indeed, many of the people, if they wanted proof for their marriages today, would not find anyone to establish the testimony regarding their matter, and I do not see any harm in what he has done, and if he bears witness, that is better.'

key_terms.رَجْعَتِهَا: Revocation of divorce / taking back the wife
key_terms.يُشْهِدْ: To bear witness / to appoint witnesses

ai.seo_question: Is a revocation of divorce (raj'a) valid without witnesses in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) ruled that a man who divorces his wife once and then takes her back before her waiting period (iddah) expires without witnesses is still married to her. While bearing witness is recommended (mustahabb) and befitting, the marriage remains valid even if he was ignorant of this requirement, though doing so is better.
